X 早报 · 2026-11-22（周日）

概览

美股经历 2020 年以来最剧烈的抛售后迎来周末：标普 500 收于 50 日均线下方 4.1 个标准差，超卖程度超过 2008 年和 2020 年，纳指 100 跌入熊市，VIX 收于 35 以上，对冲基金录得“解放日”以来最差单周表现。全球同步下跌，台股单周暴跌约 18%、创 35 年最差，台湾自周一起实施 2015 年以来首次全面限空；中国 10 月社零仅增 0.4%、固投大降，外资持有美债继续减少。AI 链上，Anthropic IPO 后现金达 2370 亿美元，马斯克警告明年 AI 行业现金将极度紧张，摩根大通 CDS 数据把 AI 巨头按融资能力分成三档，英伟达远期市盈率跌至约 8 倍。比特币跌至约 5.7 万美元，成为史上最长熊市，黄金创 13 个月新低；政治面上，参议院结束伊朗战争投票再度失败，特朗普转发“TrumpCare”并誓言将信用卡利率封顶 10%，中文圈则复盘了共和党中期选举惨败对市场的连锁冲击。本周感恩节缩短交易周，PCE 与三季度 GDP 将于周三公布。

史诗级超卖：美股恐慌与反弹信号

The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)

美股很少出现如此严重的超卖：
标普 500 本周收盘时低于其 50 日均线 4.1 个标准差，为 2015 年 8 月以来最大偏离。
这也是至少 20 年来第三大偏离。
相比之下，2008 年金融危机期间，该指数相对 50 日均线的最大偏离为 3.6 个标准差。
即便是 2020 年疫情崩盘，也没有出现如此极端的超卖，当年 2 月标普 500 跌至 50 日均线下方 3.8 个标准差。
在 2022 年熊市和 2025 年 4 月“解放日”之后的抛售中，标普 500 分别跌至 50 日均线下方 3.2 和 3.3 个标准差。
这是历史上最剧烈的市场抛售之一。

原文：US stocks have rarely been this oversold:
The S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, its widest deviation since August 2015.
This also marks its 3rd-largest deviation in at least 20 years.
By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, the index’s largest deviation from its 50-DMA was 3.6 standard deviations.
Not even the 2020 Pandemic crash saw such extreme oversold conditions, with the S&P 500 falling 3.8 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average in February.
During the 2022 bear market and the April 2025 post-"Liberation Day" selloff, the S&P 500 fell 3.2 and 3.3 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, respectively.
This has been one of the sharpest market sell-offs in history.

标普 500 刚刚经历了 2025 年 4 月以来最糟糕的一周。纳斯达克经历了 2020 年 3 月以来最糟糕的一周。英伟达单日暴跌 14%。
而我并不恐慌。下面说说到底发生了什么，以及原因。
是几件事同时袭来。
1. 英伟达
这家撑起整轮 AI 行情的公司 9 天前失去了 CEO。此后：股东诉讼、加州的传票、据报道的 SEC 调查，以及周五又有报道称监管机构正在审查其会计账目。
当市场上最大的股票单日下跌 14%，所有与之相关的东西都会跟着下跌。仅周五一天，芯片股就跌了超过 10%。
2. 美联储
所有人都预期今年会降息。结果美联储却在加息。一位美联储理事甚至说，他们可能需要在 12 月用一次 50 个基点的加息来“震慑大家”，摩根大通现在预计接下来三次会议都会加息。
利率上升对科技股打击最大。
3. 对 AI 的怀疑
投资者开始质疑，投入数据中心的数千亿美元究竟能否收回。很多人原本寄望 Anthropic 的 IPO 能把买家拉回来。结果它上市首日从 115 美元跌到了 97 美元。
4. 被迫抛售
高盛表示，趋势跟踪基金在过去一个月卖出了 570 亿美元股票，如果价格继续下跌，还可能再卖出最多 800 亿美元。
这些基金不看盈利。它们卖出是因为价格在跌，而它们的抛售又把价格压得更低。
那我为什么不恐慌？
标普目前比历史高点低约 10%。这是一次回调。回调经常发生，大多数人一年后就忘了。
纳斯达克 100 现在的估值约为明年盈利的 18 倍，比 2022 年熊市底部还便宜。
高盛的恐慌指标达到 10 分中的 9 分。高盛自己也说过，当恐慌达到如此极端时，中期前景通常会改善。
而且这轮抛售很大一部分来自自动运行的基金，而不是企业突然崩溃。
还会更低吗？会。短期内很可能还会。我不会假装知道底在哪里。
但我做这行已经 10 多年了，每次感觉像现在这样时，保持冷静的人都比在底部卖出的人好得多。
如果你害怕，就少做点。不要全部卖掉，也不要全仓梭哈。慢慢买，留些现金，别每 10 分钟就看一次账户。
我会持续更新。
很多人会后悔没有关注我。

原文：The S&P 500 just had its worst week since April 2025. The Nasdaq had its worst week since March 2020. Nvidia fell 14% in a single day.
And I'm not panicking. Here's what's really going on, and why.
It's a few things hitting at the same time.
1. Nvidia
The company that carried this entire AI run lost its CEO 9 days ago. Since then: shareholder lawsuits, a subpoena from California, a reported SEC probe, and on Friday, a report that regulators are now looking at its accounting.
When the biggest stock in the market drops 14% in a day, everything connected to it goes down too. Chip stocks fell more than 10% on Friday alone.
2. The Fed
Everyone expected rate cuts this year. Instead, the Fed is raising rates. One Fed governor even said they might need to "shock people" with a half-point hike in December, and JPMorgan now expects hikes at the next three meetings.
Higher rates hit tech stocks the hardest.
3. AI doubts
Investors are starting to ask whether the hundreds of billions going into data centers will ever pay off. A lot of people hoped the Anthropic IPO would bring buyers back. Instead, it went from $115 to $97 on its first day.
4. Forced selling
Goldman Sachs says trend-following funds sold $57 billion in stocks over the past month and could sell up to $80 billion more if prices keep falling.
These funds don't look at earnings. They sell because prices are falling, and their selling pushes prices even lower.
So why am I not panicking?
The S&P is about 10% below its record. That's a correction. They happen all the time, and most people forget about them a year later.
The Nasdaq 100 now trades at about 18x next year's earnings. That's cheaper than the bottom of the 2022 bear market.
Goldman's panic gauge is at 9 out of 10. Goldman itself has said that when panic gets this extreme, the medium-term outlook usually improves.
And a big chunk of this selling is coming from funds that run on autopilot, not from businesses suddenly falling apart.
Could it go lower? Yes. Short term, it probably will. I'm not going to pretend I know where the bottom is.
But I've been doing this for over 10 years, and every time it felt like this, the people who stayed calm did a lot better than the people who sold at the bottom.
If you're scared, do less. Don't sell everything. Don't go all in either. Buy slowly, keep some cash and stop checking your portfolio every 10 minutes.
I'll keep you updated.
A lot of people will regret not following me.

那为什么全世界会同时发生这种事？
每个国家都是同样两个原因：AI 和利率。
全球股市很大一部分都押在芯片和 AI 公司上（尤其是台湾、韩国和日本）。而现在美联储看起来准备再次加息。糟糕的组合。
这是“大崩盘”吗？我不知道。没人知道，任何说自己知道的人都在骗你。
我知道的是，周五整个标普 500 里只有大约 123 只股票上涨。在这样的日子里，人们因为害怕会把一切都卖掉，好公司和坏公司一起卖。
我入行已经 10 多年，经历过几次这种情况。每一次都感觉像世界末日。而每一次都不是。
我手上仍有一大笔现金，正在慢慢加仓。不着急。

但你们需要关注我并打开通知，这非常重要……
很多人会后悔没有关注我。

原文：🚨 READ THIS BEFORE THE MARKET OPENS ON MONDAY
$17 TRILLION was just wiped out of global stocks.
And if you think this is only an American problem, wait until you see what happened in the rest of the world this week…
I went through every major market. There's almost nowhere left to hide.
Taiwan: down 17.5% in ONE week. Its worst week since 1991.
Japan: Nikkei down 7.7%. SoftBank lost 14.5% in a single day.
South Korea: down 8%.
Europe: worst week since March. Germany alone lost more than 7%.
China: AI stocks there have lost $1.7 trillion since June. Hong Kong tech is at a 2 year low.
US: the Dow just had its worst week since covid.
Global stocks have now fallen 7 days in a row. Last time that happened was 2023.
But that's not even what bothers me the most…
Usually when stocks crash, the money runs somewhere. Gold, bitcoin, something.
This time gold is falling too, it's under $3,600. Bitcoin touched $57K. Even copper got sold.
When everything drops at the same time, it usually means people are selling whatever they can just to get cash.
So why is this happening everywhere at once?
Same 2 reasons in every country: AI and interest rates.
A huge part of the world's stock markets was riding on chip and AI companies (Taiwan, Korea and Japan especially). And now the Fed looks ready to raise rates again. Bad combo.
Is this the big one? I don't know. Nobody does, and anyone who says they know is lying to you.
What I do know is that on Friday only about 123 stocks in the whole S&P 500 went up. On days like that people sell everything, good companies and bad ones together, because they're scared.
I started over 10 years ago and I've seen a few of these. It feels like the end of the world every single time. And every time, it wasn't.
I still have a big pile of cash and I'm adding slowly. No rush.
I’ll keep you guys updated on my next move.
But you need to follow me with notifications this is VERY important…
A lot of people will regret not following me.

原文：Where I was wrong $NVDA 🩸
A couple of weeks ago, I thought the $170 to $160 support level would hold.
It broke much faster than I expected.
Last week, I said that if $160 broke, my worst case was a move down toward $120. That’s where we are now.
The volume gap from about $175 down to about $130 has filled. Price closed Friday at $125.53, approaching my worst-case zone of $110 to $120.
The SEC report
On Friday, Reuters reported that the SEC’s enforcement staff is looking into potential accounting issues at NVIDIA, citing two unnamed people briefed on the matter.
The stock fell about 14% that day, wiping out roughly $491 billion in value.
Here’s what’s actually known, and what isn’t:
It’s a reported investigation, not charges.
No fraud allegations or charges have been made public.
Reuters couldn’t determine when the inquiry started or which accounting issues it covers.
NVIDIA didn’t immediately comment, and the SEC declined to comment.
As Reuters points out, investigations aren’t evidence of wrongdoing, and many close without any enforcement action.
We talked about this risk last week in my Weekly Watchlist writeup
Michael Burry flagged NVIDIA’s switch to reporting revenue by customer headquarters, which made Singapore disappear from its geographic breakdown.
And in my earnings checklist, I asked whether NVIDIA was helping fund the demand that buys its chips.
Reuters mentions both as background concerns, but it doesn’t say either one is part of the SEC’s inquiry.
On this week’s earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress said NVIDIA would be “far more selective” about AI financing deals.
If it comes out that the company has done something wrong, this could get a lot worse.
Until then, it’s an open question, not a verdict.
Why $110 to $120 is my worst case
It’s the weekly smart money zone.
Measured from the $86 swing low, the zone sits right at $110 to $120.
It’s extremely oversold. Price is now well below the monthly smart money band, the strongest band we have, which holds about 85% of the time.
There’s a huge point of control at about $118.
The point of control is the price where the most shares have traded on the volume profile, so it tends to act as strong support.
In my opinion, price bottoms somewhere between here and about $110. That’s about 12% below Friday’s close.
What I expect short term
A relief rally is on the horizon. I think there’s a really good chance the short-term bottom forms between $120 and $125.
From there, a bounce of about 30% to 40%, back to $170, filling the volume profile.
Then one more short-term rejection at the weekly smart money band and the $170 resistance.
The bigger picture
I think we’re approaching a very long-term bottom. If I wanted to own NVIDIA for the next year, this is an insane place to do it.
But that doesn’t mean price bounces and runs back to all-time highs in a couple of weeks. I think a bounce is coming, and I think the bottom is forming. I’m just not expecting a push to all-time highs in the next couple of months.

原文：US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 1980s.
Net equity inflows measure foreign purchases of US stocks minus US investors' purchases of foreign equities.
This figure has risen nearly +5.0 percentage points since the 2022 bear market low.
Meanwhile, net debt inflows, which measure foreign purchases of US debt securities, such as Treasuries minus US purchases of foreign debt securities, are down to ~1.8%, their lowest since 2022.
As a result, net equity inflows have surpassed net debt inflows as a % of GDP by the widest margin since the 2008 Financial Crisis.
In other words, foreign investors are increasingly directing money towards US equities rather than US bonds.
Overseas demand for US equities has never been this strong.

关于我在 @TomorrowXSummit 上的所见所闻，几点想法：
1) 正如许多人已经指出的，会上机构投资者对 AI 交易普遍持谨慎和看空态度（科技从业者和个人投资者往往更乐观）。不过，虽然我听到了一大堆看空论点，但考虑到当前估值已经计入了大幅的资本开支削减，我认为只有两个论点真正站得住脚：
A) 近期对 $ANT 推理收入和算力的估算表明，我们需要的算力（GW）将远少于目前计划建设的规模。
B) 前沿实验室 ARR 增速近期放缓，表明产生的收入将不足以支撑计划中的资本开支。
我认为第一个论点往往依赖可疑的数字——例如，认为 Anthropic 只需 500MW 推理容量就能产生 1000 亿美元收入，而实际上他们今天可能正在用 1.2–1.3GW 来实现 800 亿美元的总 ARR。更重要的是，它忽略了 Anthropic 将超过 60% 的算力用于训练——以及为什么这个比例在 2027 年可能不会下降多少，甚至完全不降——也忽略了为什么竞争对手前沿实验室和开源权重模型的收入/推理 GW 数据可能大不相同（就 OpenAI 而言，它可能依靠超过 2GW 的推理算力来产生约 700 亿美元的总 ARR）。
在我看来第二个看空论点更有力，因为明年资本开支可能在 1.5 万亿美元左右，而编程相关的增长正在放缓。尽管如此，我认为执着于 OAI/Ant 第四季度 ARR 增速，忽略了以下几点：
A) 在计入开源权重模型和其他专有模型、科技巨头内部的 AI 使用、互联网公司和 ISV、本地 AI 部署等之后，OAI/Ant 似乎只占非中国 AI 算力消耗的 25–30%。
B) 开源权重模型的 token 消耗今年爆发得有多猛（从 OpenRouter、Fireworks 等的数据来看，同比增长远超 10 倍）。
C) 许多非编程工作负载（知识/企业工作、网络安全、研发等）的采用曲线似乎还处于多么早期的阶段。
D) OAI/Ant 的算力承诺、资产负债表和大模型进展，使它们不太可能因为一两个季度的 ARR 增长放缓而大幅改变资本开支计划。
E) 云巨头们每季度报告的内容以及对未来几年的信号（$AMZN 指引 2027 年和 2028 年 AWS 增速均超过 40%，而此前它从未给出超过一个季度的指引，这一点尤其值得注意）。
F) 过去的资本开支热潮（铁路、工厂、光纤等）通常是在供应/产能远远超前于需求多年之后才结束，而不是在供应只是适度超前于需求之后就结束（当然，目前连这种情况都还没出现）。
与此同时，虽然我听到了大量看空论点，但我提出的各种看多论点（涉及 token/云增长、GPU 价格、未来非编程领域的采用、大模型进展等）受到的反驳比我预想的要少。再加上我听到和无意中听到的各种想回避 AI 基础设施的非基本面原因（例如想锁定全年收益、不想冒跑输同行/基准的风险等），让我觉得最近看到的很多悲观情绪，来自投资者被近期的价格走势吓到/搅乱，于是试图事后为这种走势找理由，就像今年早些时候 SaaS 和互联网股票那样。
2) 密切关注大模型进展的人对明年将出现重大突破的乐观程度令人瞩目。我听到多个预测称明年将实现 RSI（递归自我改进）（可以说各实验室已经实现了部分 RSI——参见 METR 最近关于 Anthropic 大模型进展速度的报告），以及能够在各类机器人任务/环境中完全泛化的大模型将在 2027 年出现。
对于通用机器人/人形机器人而言，硬件工程可能很快就会成为大规模部署的最大剩余障碍。我目前没有把机器人拐点纳入对半导体的预期，这类事情通常也不会一夜之间发生，但如果/当它真的发生，对内存、算力、功率半导体、传感器等显然会有重大影响。
3) 与科技/产品人士关于企业 AI 采用（无论是整体还是其中某部分）的交流让我认为，短期内采用率很可能起伏不定、参差不齐——这种起伏当然也符合 Ant/OAI 近期 ARR 增速放缓的情况。但他们也给出了对更长时间维度保持乐观的理由。
目前，相对少数的早期采用者/重度用户（在公司、部门/团队和个人层面）贡献了非编程 token 增长的很大一部分。而且我的印象是，相当多的公司（尤其是科技和金融以外的公司）仍处于试错阶段，试图弄清楚哪些 AI 项目有、哪些没有很强的投资回报，以及如何让 token 支出物有所值。
与此同时，我听到了一些有趣的案例：AI 被用于分析海量且频繁变化的数据集并从中发现洞见、加速/改进芯片设计、帮助办公室员工处理大得多的工作量等。AlphaSense 表示其 token 消耗年化已达 80 万亿（自年初以来增长 8 倍），而且这还是在其使用量严重偏向重度用户的情况下（据称其 SuperAnalyst 工具前 1% 用户消耗的 token 是中位用户的 28 倍）。
另外，我认为如果假设非编程领域的大量 token 使用会永远局限于少数早期采用者/重度用户，那将是个错误。一方面因为大模型和应用开发者非常清楚这个问题，正在努力提升普通用户的使用量；另一方面因为大模型最近在处理复杂的知识/企业任务方面进步很大——明年还会有更大的进展，尤其是如果 RSI 实现的话——这应该会为 IT 部门和重度用户全面自动化各种智能体任务和工作流铺平道路。
——
总的来说，这次会议强化了我的观点：如果可以把 AI 热潮中的市场走势与互联网泡沫时代相比，那么最近的抛售更可能被视为类似 1998 年夏秋（当时纳斯达克从 7 月中旬到 10 月初下跌超过 30%，伴随动量急剧反转、宏观担忧和基金爆仓，一度年内转跌，随后狂欢继续），而不是类似 2000 年秋天（那时狂欢彻底结束）。
话虽如此，就估值/财务状况、技术/生产力进步和企业支出增长而言，我认为 AI 热潮与互联网/电信热潮的共同点，可能不如与 80 年代末至 90 年代初中期的 PC 和客户端/服务器热潮多——当时“智能”（以 CPU MIPS 衡量）成本的持续下降，被用户增长加上更先进软件和工作负载的资源需求所抵消，而且绰绰有余。

原文：A few thoughts on what I saw and heard at the @TomorrowXSummit:
1) As many others have noted, cautious and bearish views on the AI trade abounded at the conference among institutional investors (tech people and individual investors were often more bullish). But while I heard a slew of bearish arguments, I thought only two really carried weight given the massive capex cuts priced in by current valuations:
A) That recent $ANT inference revenue and compute estimates suggest we’ll need far fewer GW of compute than what’s currently set to be built.
B) That the recent slowdown in frontier lab ARR growth suggests we won’t see enough revenue generated to justify planned capex.
I think the first argument often relies on questionable numbers – for example, a belief that Anthropic only needs 500MW in inference capacity to produce $100B in revenue, when they might actually be using 1.2-1.3GW today to achieve $80B in gross ARR. And more importantly, it glosses over Anthropic dedicating over 60% of its compute to training -- and why that number might not decline much, if at all, in 2027 -- and why revenue/inference GW numbers probably look very different for rival frontier labs and open-weight models (for its part, OpenAI might be relying on over 2GW in inference to produce ~$70B in gross ARR).
The second bear argument is stronger IMO given that capex might be around $1.5T next year and coding-related growth is slowing down. That said, I think fixating on Q4 OAI/Ant ARR growth overlooks:
A) How OAI/Ant appear to make up just 25-30% of non-China AI compute consumption, after accounting for open-weight and rival proprietary models, internal AI usage among the tech giants, Internet firms and ISVs, local AI deployments, etc.
B) How much (judging by data from OpenRouter, Fireworks, etc.) open-weight token consumption has exploded this year (looks like it’s up well over 10x Y/Y).
C) How early we appear to be in the adoption curve for many non-coding workloads (knowledge/enterprise work, cyber, R&D, etc.).
D) How OAI/Ant’s compute commitments, balance sheets and LLM progress make them unlikely to meaningfully change their capex plans in response to a quarter or two of slow ARR growth.
E) What the cloud giants are both reporting quarterly as well as signaling for the next couple of years ($AMZN guiding for 40%+ AWS growth in both 2027 and 2028, after having previously never guided more than a quarter out, seems especially notable).
F) How past capex booms (railroads, factories, fiber, etc.) typically ended only after years of supply/capacity being well ahead of demand, rather than after supply got just moderately ahead of demand (and of course, even that’s not the case right now).
Meanwhile, though I heard plenty of bearish arguments, I got less pushback than I thought I would for various bullish arguments (related to token/cloud growth, GPU prices, future non-coding adoption, LLM progress, etc.). That, together with all the non-fundamental reasons I heard and overheard for wanting to avoid AI infra (e.g. wanting to lock in gains for the year, not wanting to risk underperforming peers/benchmarks, etc.), made me think a lot of the negativity we’ve seen lately comes from investors being frightened/unsettled by recent price action and thus trying to rationalize that price action ex-post, much as we saw with SaaS and Internet stocks earlier this year.
2) The optimism from people closely monitoring LLM progress about major advances happening next year was notable. I heard multiple predictions that RSI would be achieved next year (one could argue the labs have already achieved partial RSI – see METR’s recent report on the pace of Anthropic LLM advances), as well as that LLMs capable of fully generalizing across robotics tasks/environments would arrive in 2027.
With general-purpose robots/humanoids, it looks like hardware engineering might soon be the biggest remaining obstacle to mass deployment. I’m not currently baking a robotics inflection into my expectations for semis, and stuff like this usually doesn’t transpire overnight, but if/when it does happen, there are obviously big implications for memory, compute, power semis, sensors, etc.
3) Talks with tech/product people about enterprise AI adoption (whether in aggregate or some part of it) made me think we’ll likely see choppy/uneven adoption rates in the short-term -- and such choppiness of course fits with Ant/OAI’s recent ARR growth slowdowns. But they also provided reasons to be optimistic about what happens over longer timeframes.
For now, a relatively small number of early adopters/power users (at the corporate, department/team and individual levels) are driving a huge % of non-coding token growth. And I get the impression that quite a few companies (esp. outside of tech and finance) are still in the trial-and-error stage, trying to figure out which AI projects do and don’t have strong ROIs and how to get the most bang for their buck from their token spend.
At the same time, I heard interesting anecdotes about AI being used to analyze/uncover insights from massive and frequently-changing datasets, accelerate/improve chip design, help office workers handle much larger workloads, etc. AlphaSense said its token consumption is now up to 80T annualized (up 8x since the start of the year), and that’s even though its usage skews heavily towards power users (the top 1% of users for their SuperAnalyst tool were said to consume 28x as many tokens as the median user).
Also, I think it’d be a mistake to assume heavy non-coding token usage remains limited to a small number of early adopters/power users forever. Both because LLM and app developers are well-aware of this issue and trying hard to drive higher usage among normies, and because LLMs have been getting much better lately at handling complex knowledge/enterprise tasks – with bigger advances due next year, especially if RSI arrives – which should pave the way for IT departments and power users fully automating various agentic tasks and workflows.
—
On the whole, the conference strengthened my view that – to the extent one can compare market action during the AI boom to that of the Dotcom era – the recent selloff is more likely to go down as something comparable to the summer/fall of 1998 (when the Nasdaq fell over 30% from mid-July to early October amid a sharp momentum reversal, macro worries and fund blowups, and briefly went red for the year, before the party resumed) than something comparable to the fall of 2000 (when the party ended of good).
That said, in terms of valuations/financials, tech/productivity advances and corporate spending growth, I think the AI boom might have less in common with the Internet/telco boom than with the PC and client/server boom of the late '80s and early/mid ‘90s, when steady declines in the cost of “intelligence” (as defined by CPU MIPS) were more than offset by a combo of user growth and the resource demands of more advanced software and workloads.

原文：Ray Dalio explains how market bubbles form:
"The bubble, the mechanics of it, is that people mistake a great new technology for a great investment."
"Everything depends on AI, right? The markets, the economy, everything depends on AI. And so that technology is volatile and very risky."
Dalio explains that when everyone believes in a new technology, investors often borrow money to gain exposure, driving up demand and creating enormous wealth.
The problem starts when investors need cash, whether to repay debt, cover higher interest costs or pay taxes. They're forced to sell assets, even if they still believe in the technology.
As selling accelerates, confidence turns into fear, investors pull back, and the same forces that drove prices higher begin working in reverse.

2013: Icahn peaks at $26.1B, one of the 25 richest people in the world. Almost all of it is one stock, Icahn Enterprises (IEP). He owns about 87% of it.
2014 to 2022: His funds lose money in 7 out of 9 years. He keeps betting on a market crash that never comes.
2017 to early 2023: Those short bets alone lose close to $9 BILLION. He later admitted to the Financial Times it was a mistake.
2018: He starts borrowing billions personally against his IEP stock. The SEC later said he never properly disclosed it.
May 2, 2023: Hindenburg Research calls IEP's dividend "Ponzi-like". IEP was paying $8 a year per unit while losing money. The stock falls 20% that day and his net worth drops over $10B in ONE day, to $14.6B. Within a month the stock is down more than half.
July 2023: He restructures about $3.7B of personal loans so they're no longer tied to the stock price.
August 2023: IEP cuts the dividend in half. The stock drops 23% in a day.
August 2024: Icahn and IEP pay the SEC $2M over the undisclosed loans, without admitting or denying anything.
November 2024: The dividend gets cut in half AGAIN, to $0.50 a quarter.
July 2026: He bids $34 a share for Caesars. The board sticks with Tilman Fertitta's LOWER $31 offer because it trusted his financing more.
September 2026: Icahn falls off the Forbes 400 for the first time in 40 years.
Q3 2026: His funds lose 31% in one quarter, mostly on hedges against refining stocks.
November 3, 2026: CVR Energy, IEP's biggest holding, announces a $4.2B deal to buy 2 refineries. CVR is down about 40% since. The same day IEP reports earnings and warns it can't promise to refinance the $1.4B of bonds due in May.
November 16: IEP falls 24% in a single day.
Where it stands now:
- IEP closed at $2.73 on Tuesday. It was around $50 before Hindenburg
- it's down 64% this year
- the May bonds yield over 14%. Three months ago it was about 6%
- some of its 2029 bonds yield over 30%
- Icahn still has about $1.3B of personal loans, with his ENTIRE IEP stake pledged, plus properties in the Hamptons and New York City
And IEP still pays that dividend. About $380M a quarter on paper, a yield of over 70%. Icahn takes only about $25M of his in cash and the rest in new units.
To be fair: IEP had $921M of cash and $1.4B in its funds at the end of September, and it's selling Pep Boys for about $700M. It plans to pay the May bonds with cash, new debt or money from the funds. Icahn has also disputed Forbes' estimates of his wealth.
Forbes did the math on this. If he had put his $26B into the S&P 500 in 2014 and never touched it, he'd have over $130 BILLION today.

The company explained that because transactions are conducted through various methods such as deposits, it is difficult to judge long term agreements based on contract liabilities or advance payments alone. However, escrow, guarantees, and collateral are arrangements where money can only be recovered through set procedures if a contract is broken. If the company had truly strengthened the binding force of its agreements, there should be some other reason for choosing these methods over receiving advance payments directly. One accountant also noted that escrow is not a common arrangement, pointing out that a company can earn at least interest simply by receiving the money directly and putting it to work, so there is no reason to deposit it with a third party.
Samsung Electronics is in a different situation. Its contract liabilities, which had stayed within a set range for several years, rose by about KRW 8.5 trillion quarter on quarter in the second quarter of this year to KRW 23.6 trillion as it signed long term agreements with large customers. The company said advance payments would grow further as additional contracts were signed. In the third quarter, however, contract liabilities related to advance payments rose by only about KRW 550 billion. The industry believes Samsung may have reduced the amount of upfront payments in the additional contracts in exchange for raising the price cap on semiconductors. If this interpretation is correct, it does not match the company's description of "sufficiently binding LTAs." This is because lower advance payments make it easier for customers to walk away from contracts if the memory supply and demand balance reverses.

原文：Inflationary is intensifying in Japan:
Japan’s Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) jumped +4.2% YoY in October, its largest annual increase since 1990, and far above expectations of +3.6%.
This index tracks domestic prices businesses charge each other for services, and serves as a key inflation metric in Japan.
MoM, the index rose +1.1%, up from +0.3% in the previous month and marking its biggest monthly increase in 6 months.
The latest surge was driven particularly by higher ocean freight transportation costs, leasing costs, and hotel charges.
Prices in transport and postal activities alone jumped +9.4% YoY in October, following an +8.4% increase in September.
Rising inflationary pressures are strengthening the case for a December rate hike by the Bank of Japan.

安联：“迄今为止，这轮抛售看起来更像是拥挤仓位的平仓，而不是 AI 投资逻辑的根本性破裂。”
三个负面催化因素：
英伟达 CEO 更替、美国国会措施，以及国际上对英伟达芯片获取的限制，引发了不成比例的大规模抛售
- 散户热门股受冲击最大，因为这轮抛售主要是拥挤仓位的平仓
（这或许可以解释 $NBIS、$SIVE、$ASTS、$IREN、$HOOD 以及其他散户热门股最近的走势）。
- 对冲基金：拥挤仓位同样承受了更大的抛售压力。
- 信贷市场：美国高收益债券当周跌幅不到 1%，表明信贷压力相对可控。
“担忧是合理的（变现担忧、政治因素、增长见顶（而非盈利见顶）），但风险被高估了——估值方面：AI 交易又变便宜了。
下一个考验是这种疲软是否会蔓延到信贷、资本开支和更广泛的经济。”
“因此我们的基本判断是，这主要是一次仓位的平仓。”
我个人能在亚洲新云厂商和个别供应商身上找到负面信号，并将其泛化到整个 AI 交易上。
但我和许多行业高管的看法一致：从算力到网络，底层的基本面需求依然永不满足。
考虑到股票估值已经重置，进入 2027 年我在方向上看多。

原文：Allianz: "The sell-off has so far looked more like an unwind of crowded positions than a fundamental break in the AI investment case."
Three negative catalysts from:
$NVDA CEO change, US congressional measures, and restrictions Nvidia chips access internationally, triggered a disproportionately large sell-off
- Retail-popular stocks were hit hardest because the sell-off was primarily an unwinding of crowded positions
(this could possibly explain $NBIS, $SIVE, $ASTS, $IREN, $HOOD and other retail favorite price action recently).
- Hedge funds: Crowded positions also experienced greater selling pressure.
- Credit markets: US high-yield bonds lost less than 1% during the week, suggesting relatively contained credit stress.
"Legitimate concerns [monetization concerns, politics, growth peak (not earnings)], but overdone risks valuation: AI trade is cheap again.
The next test will be whether the weakness spreads to credit, capital spending and the broader economy."
"Our working view is therefore that this is mainly a positioning unwind."
I can personally find negative signals across Asian Neoclouds and individual suppliers and extrapolate those broadly to the entire AI trade.
But I share the perspective of many industry executives that underlying fundamental demand from compute to networking remains insatiable.
Given the equity valuation reset, directionally bullish entering 2027

好好想了下当时市场对雷曼CDS定价相对滞后的原因是当时雷曼很多风险藏在表外和复杂结构化产品里，市场看不清。同时对于这种“大而不能倒”的金融机构市场还有政府会出手救助的期待。

本质上现在市场是在提前为“杠杆AI模式可能走不通”这个情景定价，而不是在定价已经发生的违约。

关于华为在 ISSCC 上发布的 HBM 工作的几点想法。
我把它看作华为以类似 Tau 的方式绕开 EUV 瓶颈。中国终于绕过 JEDEC，走自己的路了。
如果这真的可行，华为可以在 HBM3 级别的引脚速率下实现 HBM4 级别的单堆栈带宽。没有 EUV 级别的 DRAM 微缩，就很难进一步提升 HBM 引脚速率。所以华为干脆走了一条完全不同的路线。
晶圆级混合键合也是中国的强项。（长江存储也采用晶圆对晶圆，即 W2W 混合键合。）
我觉得特别有意思的是，包括三星在内的西方生态系统中的 HBM 厂商，会用台积电 3nm 这样的先进代工节点来做逻辑 die，以实现高引脚速率。华为在这两方面都受到限制：它的 DRAM 微缩走不了那么远，也拿不到先进的代工节点。所以它选择做得更宽，以弥补这些工艺上的限制。
当然，如果事情这么简单，三星早就这么做了。W2W 的一大缺点是无法在堆叠前剔除单个有缺陷的 die，因此各层的良率会相乘。
假设每层良率为 95%，堆叠五层后良率就降到 77%。
而 95% 已经是相当乐观的假设了。如果每层良率是 70%，五层堆叠的良率就只剩 17%。那简直是灾难。
更痛苦的是，这会吃掉中国本就有限的 DRAM 晶圆供应。晶粒对晶圆（D2W）键合可以在堆叠前挑选已知良品 die。对于五层堆叠，W2W 每个良品堆叠所用的晶圆数是 D2W 的 1/y⁴ 倍，其中 y 为每层良率。在堆叠良率为 77% 时，W2W 用的晶圆是 D2W 的 1.23 倍；在 17% 时，则跃升到惊人的 4.16 倍。
换句话说，在那种情形下，中国制造一个 HBM 堆叠所需的晶圆要比 SK 海力士多四倍以上。这意味着中国需要韩国和美光合计 DRAM 产能的四倍以上，才能匹配美国 AI 加速器的出货量。（这是最坏的情形。）
不过，这仍是一种非常有意思的思路。感觉中国和西方的技术标准正在逐渐分化，就像冷战时期苏联和西方的标准那样。

原文：A few thoughts on Huawei’s HBM work at ISSCC.
I see it as Huawei’s Tau-style way around the EUV bottleneck. China is finally bypassing JEDEC and going its own way.
If this actually works, Huawei could get HBM4-class bandwidth per stack at HBM3-class pin speeds. Without EUV-class DRAM scaling, it’s hard to push HBM pin speeds higher. So Huawei is taking a different route altogether.
Wafer-scale hybrid bonding is also an area where China is strong. (YMTC uses wafer-to-wafer, or W2W, hybrid bonding too.)
What I find especially interesting is that HBM makers in the Western ecosystem, including Samsung, use leading-edge foundry nodes like TSMC’s 3nm for their logic dies to hit high pin speeds. Huawei is constrained on both fronts. It can’t scale its DRAM as far, and it doesn’t have access to leading-edge foundry nodes. So it’s going wider to make up for those process limitations.
Of course, if it were that simple, Samsung would have done it already. The big drawback with W2W is that you can’t exclude individual defective dies before stacking, so the yields of the individual layers multiply.
Say each layer has a 95% yield. Stack five layers and the yield drops to 77%.
And 95% is already a pretty optimistic assumption. At 70% per layer, the yield for a five-layer stack drops to just 17%. That’s a disaster.
What makes this even more painful is that it eats into China’s already limited supply of DRAM wafers. Die-to-wafer (D2W) bonding lets you select known-good dies before stacking. For a five-layer stack, W2W uses 1/y⁴ times as many wafers per good stack as D2W, where y is the yield per layer. At a stack yield of 77%, W2W uses 1.23× as many wafers as D2W. At 17%, that jumps to a whopping 4.16×.
In other words, in that scenario, China would need more than four times as many wafers as SK hynix to make a single HBM stack. That would mean China needs more than four times the combined DRAM production capacity of South Korea and Micron to match U.S. AI accelerator shipments. (That’s the worst-case scenario.)
Still, it’s a fascinating approach. It feels like Chinese and Western tech standards are gradually diverging, much like Soviet and Western standards did during the Cold War.

有的时候我觉得，这已经不是赚钱与否、是否创造一个产品、享受乐趣这么简单的一件事。
于我而言，谁不想一起创造一个我们前所未见的、从亘古到现在都没有出现过的伟大时代呢？这样伟大的时代，不可能，也不应该仅仅属于硅谷。

原文：The most important assumption in the SALP letter is that RSI creates an oligopoly at the frontier with real pricing power. TLDR; market structure at the frontier might be the single most important variable for tech investing over the next 2-3 years.

新一期 Situational Awareness 信中充斥着同一种有缺陷的套路，这种套路在 AI 市场预测中已经非常常见：
第 1 步：严重歪曲一项业务或资产类别的本质及其定价权来源
第 2 步：宣称 AI 将取代该业务中某些看起来显眼的部分
第 3 步：“因此这项业务不再有护城河”
第 4 步：“如果你真的信 AGI，你就知道这项业务 5 年后将一文不值”
例如，Leopold 说“当今大部分房地产价值反映的是其实体建筑的价值”，而机器人将使建造成本暴跌，土地又很充足，所以房地产成本会降到零。
这是什么话……房地产的价值，尤其是高端房地产，在很大程度上由地段决定，而这是一种由区划规定和网络效应驱动的根本性稀缺，以数十年乃至数百年的尺度复利累积。仅仅降低建造成本，你不可能再造一个曼哈顿、深圳、Deer Valley 或汉普顿。事实上，相对于经济其他部分不断下降的成本，这些东西会变得不成比例地更加稀缺（参见：鲍莫尔成本病），从而推动其价格更高（与这里那个半生不熟的“AGI 信徒”结论恰恰相反）。
同样，他谈到英伟达的所有 IP/人才都会被 AI 商品化、CUDA 护城河被侵蚀，因此英伟达完蛋。这一点在方向上更站得住脚，但英伟达远不只是 CUDA/软件人才，他们拥有非常复杂而深厚的供应商网络，可能在网络技术上遥遥领先，还可能将其造芯经验/运营规模/资本规模转化为进一步复利增长的算力建设。（话虽如此，广泛做空英伟达似乎说得通，但这个分析感觉有点半生不熟。）
但总的来说，我们在很多地方都能看到这种套路。例如 Citrini 的“智能危机”一文说“DoorDash 会死，因为任何人都能写出一个 DoorDash 应用”——但应用真的是创建 DoorDash 的壁垒吗？或者更离谱的是“亚马逊会死，因为任何人都能写出亚马逊，而且智能体会替你买东西”——但亚马逊的优势难道不是它的实体物流网络吗？还有谁能稳定地在明天、甚至在 4 小时内把东西送到你手上？
关键是，许多伟大的企业拥有依然非常“抗 AGI”的结构性优势。AGI 会把任何受限于智能的东西转变为可以用算力成本替代的东西。任何以某种形式的智能（无论是像咨询那样的经验型智能，还是更偏组织/沟通流程的智能）为定价权来源的企业，确实会受到冲击。
但网络效应（尤其是实体网络）、流程能力（现实世界对信号释放/学习仍有速率限制）、法定许可（即监管）、位置稀缺性，依然是维持定价权的非常强大的力量。
（顺便说一句，这并不是要嘲讽 SALP 的信。里面依然有很多好想法。）

原文：New Situational Awareness letter is littered with many instances of the same flawed trope that has become very common in AI market predictions:
step 1. heavily mischaracterize the essence of a business or asset class and where its pricing power comes from
step 2. declare that AI will replace xyz parts of the business which seem salient
step 3. "therefore this business has no moat anymore"
step 4. "if you are really AGI pilled you know this business will be worth nothing in 5 years"
For example, Leopold says "the majority of real estate value today reflects the value of their physical structures" and that robotics will crash the cost of building structures and there's plenty of land to build stuff so cost of real estate drops to zero.
What... the value of real estate especially at the high end is heavily location driven and that is a fundamental scarcity driven by zoning and network effects that compound on the order of decades to centuries. You aren't going to create another Manhattan, Shenzhen, Deer Valley, Hamptons with just dropping construction costs. In fact, those things will become disproportionately more scarce with respect to the rest of the economy's dropping costs (see: Baumol's cost disease), driving their prices even higher (opposite of the half baked "AGI pilled" conclusion here.
Similarly he talks about all of NVIDIA's IP/talent being commoditized by AI and CUDA moat eroded therefore rip NVIDIA. This one is more directionally valid but also NVIDIA is much more than just CUDA/software talent, they have very complex and deep supplier networks, are potentially far ahead on networking technology, may be able to compound their chip building expertise/operational scale/capital scale into farther compounding compute buildout. (that being said, being short NVIDIA broadly seems valid, but the analysis feels a bit half baked)
But in general we see this trope in a lot of places. Ex: the Citrini Intelligence Crisis post "DoorDash dies because anyone can code a DoorDash app" - but was the app really the barrier to creating DoorDash? Or more egregiously "Amazon dies because anyone can code Amazon and agents will be buying stuff for you" - but wasn't Amazons edge their physical logistics network? Who else can deliver something to you consistently by tomorrow, or maybe even within the next 4 hours?
The point is, many of the great businesses have structural advantages that are still very AGI proof. AGI converts anything bottlenecked by intelligence to being able to substitute for the cost of compute. Any business where intelligence of some form (whether it be experiential like consulting, or more organizational/communication flows based) is the source of pricing power will suffer, yes.
But network effects (especially physical networks), process power (reality still has a rate limit for signal release/learning), fiat (ie. regulatory), positional scarcity still remain very powerful forces to maintain pricing power.
(Btw, this isn't meant to be a dunk on SALP letter. Many good ideas in there still.)

这是个非常好的观点，我最近在日本和美国之间往返时也意识到了这一点。
尽管经济不景气，日本的生活成本优势和生活质量依然高得惊人，因为那里的社会凝聚力极强，几乎没有犯罪。
当你去掉与犯罪相关的成本，一切都会突然便宜很多。这就是市场运作的方式。最简单的理解方式是：如果需要覆盖的风险更少，利润率就可以更低。
一家开在危险街区的商店需要摄像头、额外的员工、保安，而且仍然会被偷。它必须提价来覆盖这些成本，所以东西就更贵了。
但这只是最显眼的部分。实际上，供应链的每一个环节都需要足够的利润率来覆盖盗窃、欺诈或纯粹的不诚实行为。我记得在意大利长大时，卡车司机吹嘘自己“弄丢”了 10% 的货物是很常见的事。这意味着其他所有东西*永远*都得*至少*贵 10%，来覆盖*潜在的*损失。
每当商品或服务易手一次就加上 10% 的损耗，不诚实带来的复利效应就显而易见了。
在西方，你会看到暴徒砸毁商店橱窗，还用“没关系，他们有保险”来为自己开脱。而在日本，人们在文化上普遍理解：哪怕最小的违规行为，也会产生不利且不断累积的影响，损害到其他所有人。

原文：This is a really good point which I realized recently moving between Japan and the US
The cost of living and quality of life is just so incredibly high in Japan despite the bad economy because they have exceptionally high social cohesion and virtually no crime.
When you remove the costs associated with crime, everything becomes suddenly much much cheaper. It's just how markets work. The simplest way to understand it is that margins can be smaller if there's less risk to be covered.
A shop in a dangerous neighborhood needs cameras, extra staff, security and still has shoplifting. They'll have to raise prices to cover all of that, so things get more expensive.
But that's just the most visible part of it. In reality every step of the supply chain needs sufficient margins to cover theft, fraud, or simply dishonest behavior. I remember growing up in Italy it was common for truckers to brag about "losing" 10% of their load. That just means everything else will *always* have to cost *at least* 10% more to cover the *potential* losses
Add 10% of loss to every time goods or services change hands, and the compounding effects of dishonesty become apparent
In the west you see rioters breaking shop fronts and justifying themselves with "it doesn't matter, they're insured". In Japan it is culturally understood that even the smallest rule breaking has adverse and compounding effects that negatively affect everyone else
